articles.title: "People may lose their jobs": Thomas Müller takes brutal swipe at MLS, says players lack consistency compared to European stars
articles.summary: Thomas Müller has experienced the intensity of European football, where one poor season can cost a club its place among the elite.
articles.body: Thomas Müller has experienced the intensity of European football, where one poor season can cost a club its place among the elite. His time in Major League Soccer has offered a very different experience. The Vancouver Whitecaps forward believes the league's structure reduces the pressure on struggling teams. He has also raised concerns about player consistency, suggesting MLS still has areas to improve despite the individual talent on display.Thomas Müller questions MLS over lack of relegationThe absence of promotion and relegation is one of the biggest differences Müller has noticed between MLS and Europe's major competitions. In leagues such as the Premier League and Bundesliga, teams at the bottom face the threat of dropping into a lower division. That possibility can affect everything from club finances to players' futures.During an interview with Global News, the former Bayern Munich star explained why the pressure is not the same in North America.“It’s difficult to make a comparison because of the competition system. There’s no relegation here, and there isn’t as much pressure. A team can say it’s going through a rebuilding process. Nobody likes to lose, but it’s completely different when you’re fighting to avoid relegation,” he noted.Müller also highlighted the financial consequences of relegation, explaining how it can affect employees, players and supporters.“When a team is relegated, it loses funding for the following season, and that affects the entire organization. Some people may even lose their jobs due to the economic changes. It's also a different situation for the fans and the players, who may find themselves without a contract for the following year,” he explained.He believes the difference can also influence how teams defend, particularly when they face opponents near the bottom of the table.“That is why the style of play changes when you face a team near the bottom of the table in Europe. Those teams are fighting for survival and, sometimes, I get the feeling that because of the MLS system, football here is a little more optimistic or carefree defensively,” he said.Still, Müller acknowledged that this approach can make matches more entertaining by creating space for attacking football.Thomas Müller points out consistency issues in MLSThe German also questioned the regularity of performances across MLS. He recognised that the league has players capable of producing outstanding individual moments but believes their overall performances can vary too much.“When I compare both competitions, I see MLS players capable of producing individual moments of a very high standard. However, one thing I sometimes miss is consistency. The difference between good and bad performances is greater,” he said.Using golf as an example, Müller explained that even an amateur can occasionally produce a professional-level shot, but professionals make fewer poor attempts.He believes concentration remains a key area for improvement.“I think that sometimes what is missing is maintaining concentration and focus for all 90 minutes. That is something I have observed in MLS,” he concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Wales face Slovenia in Nations League play-off in March 2027
articles.summary: Wales will face Slovenia in a two-leg play-off next March to maintain their top-flight status in the Nations League.
articles.body:
Wales will face Slovenia in a two-leg play-off next March to maintain their top-flight status in the Nations League.

Craig Bellamy's side face the relegation play-off after finishing bottom of Group A4, while Slovenia were runners-up in B1.

The first leg will be played between March 25-27 and the second between March 28-30. Wales will have home advantage in the second leg.

The winner will play in League A for the next edition of the Nations League, while the loser will be in League B.

Wales have only played Slovenia once before, a goalless friendly in Swansea in 2005.

Slovenia lost only once in their Nations League campaign, 2-1 away to group winners Switzerland, and took four points off Scotland, who finished third.

They drew 0-0 at home against the Swiss and Scotland, who they beat 2-1 in Glasgow last month.

Bostjan Cesar's side also beat North Macedonia 2-0 at home and 3-0 away in their final game earlier this week.

Wales' only victory was 2-1 at home to Norway in October. They were beaten in Oslo and home and away by both Portugal and Denmark.

There are eight places between Wales (41st) and Slovenia (49th) in the Fifa world rankings.

Wales' Nations League campaign boosts Bellamy's belief

Portugal hold off bold Wales in five-goal thriller

Although Wales still have a chance to retain their League A status for the 2028-29 Nations League, finishing bottom in the current campaign means they will not be among the top seeds in qualifying for Euro 2028 - which includes matches in Wales as co-hosts with England, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland.

Bellamy's side could therefore be drawn alongside one of Europe's heavyweights in their qualifying group.

Spain, France, Italy, Netherlands and Portugal are among the sides already guaranteed pot one seeding for the draw on 6 December in Belfast.

England will also be a top seed, although they will be kept apart from Wales and the other Euro 2028 co-hosts in qualifying regardless.

When it comes to reaching the Euros, the 12 group winners and eight best-ranked runners-up qualify directly.

For any of the co-hosts who do not make it via that route, there are two automatic spots available. Those will be awarded to the best-ranked between the four nations who have not qualified directly.

If Wales still have not made it, there is also the back-up option of the play-offs.

And given play-off places are based on Nations League rankings, Wales are highly likely to already have that safety net.

articles.standfirst: El extremo, goleador esta temporada en Albacete y Valladolid, sufre una lesión muscular en el gemelo derecho y se pierde la cita de El Arcángel
articles.summary: El extremo, goleador esta temporada en Albacete y Valladolid, sufre una lesión muscular en el gemelo derecho y se pierde la cita de El Arcángel
articles.body: Pablo Sáenz fue uno de los primeros jugadores a los que recurrió Raúl González cuando se le torció el partido de su debut con el Oviedo. Una semana después, el técnico pierde esa opción para su primer desplazamiento al frente de los azules. Este viernes se confirmó la lesión muscular en el gemelo derecho del extremo, que será baja el domingo contra el Córdoba. A Sáenz le han sentado bien los viajes en este arranque de Liga. Fue suyo el gol que le dio los tres puntos al Oviedo en Albacete (0-1) y volvió a marcar en Valladolid, donde los asturianos ganaron por 0-3. Después encadenó tres partidos completos, frente al Sabadell, el Sporting y el Eldense. Más reciente es su aportación en Cádiz, donde jugó 29 minutos en la última victoria azul antes del relevo en el banquillo. Raúl le dio entrada en el minuto 66 ante el Girona. Apenas habían pasado dos minutos desde el 1-2 y el técnico movió dos piezas a la vez. Sáenz ocupó el sitio de Alberto Reina y Jacobo González relevó a Estanis Pedrola. Ese fue el primer intento del nuevo entrenador por rescatar un punto en el Tartiere. En El Arcángel buscará su primera victoria con tres ausencias por lesión. A la del extremo se suman las ya conocidas de Chris Ramos y Dani Calvo, bajas de larga duración. El que vuelve a entrar en los planes de Raúl es Enzo Pérez. El canterano se perdió el estreno del entrenador por su convocatoria con España sub-19, con la que debutó. Regresó en buenas condiciones después de jugar la segunda parte de la goleada a Finlandia y podrá pelear por un puesto en el once. El Oviedo completará este sábado el último entrenamiento antes de viajar a Andalucía. Volará a Málaga y cubrirá en autobús el trayecto hasta Córdoba. Allí le espera un viejo conocido de la afición azul, Iván Ania, rival de Raúl el domingo a partir de las 14.00 horas.

articles.title: The Colts should “evaluate” Shane Steichen
articles.summary: The Colts organization needs to be the one doing the evaluating at this point.
articles.body:
"We'll evaluate everything." Have you heard that before? It's becoming a canned phrase and mantra for Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen. The most recent example comes after the Colts were ripped apart by the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. That's a smart move, Shane. Maybe the Colts organization needs to do the same for you too.

The Colts sit at 3-8 on the year, and Steichen's overall record is 28-34. The man who was brought in due to his success with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia offense was unable to mold Anthony Richardson in the same fashion or create results. Zero postseason appearances and a 7-25 record when the opponent is over .500 make the case why he needs to be heavily scrutinized.

It is wise to consider benching Daniel Jones. Does it get better? Maybe not. That's on Chris Ballard and Steichen, however. Steichen had a choice between the two men at quarterback. Not that his options were necessarily glowing, but he picked Jones to be his guy. From the onset, it looked like a stroke of genius. Now, it looks disastrous. He can evaluate all he wants. The Colts organization should do the same. It isn't just Steichen, but it starts there. Based on the last four years of data, the case can be made that a change in leadership is needed.

Evaluating is normally a good thing. What can trip one up is the timing. Shane Steichen's "evaluation" of Daniel Jones and the quarterback position might be too little, too late to save his job. Steichen's time with the franchise might be drawing to a close, but the Colts organization will live on. Their time for evaluation is now. It starts with the head coach.

articles.title: Pellegrini: "Prefiero no ganar el derbi y poder jugar la Champions"
articles.standfirst: El técnico comparece tras el último entrenamiento del Betis previo a El Gran Derbi
articles.summary: El técnico comparece tras el último entrenamiento del Betis previo a El Gran Derbi
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini ha comparecido ante los medios tras el último entrenamiento del Betis previo al primer derbi de la temporada que se disputará mañana sábado (18.30 horas) en el Sánchez-Pizjuán. La cuenta atrás ha comenzado. "El equipo llega bien, veníamos con buenos resultados. El parón para nosotros fue más corto porque jugamos Copa y se fueron sumando los internacionales, pero el equipo ha entrenado bien". La clave para ganar el derbi: "Lo más importante es conseguir los tres puntos, ganar, y más un derbi. Tenemos que mantener la línea futbolística y buscar el partido desde el primer minuto. Somos visita, pero eso no altera nuestro fundamento futbolístico". No hay favorito. "Nunca lo hay, uno puede ganar los nueve derbis anteriores y perder el siguiente. Cuanto uno más se sienta favorito, es peor. El fútbol es el deporte más popular del mundo porque tiene muchas circunstancias que no da un favorito fácilmente a excepción de los equipos muy grandes, pero también son muchas las sorpresas. Es un derbi con dos equipos en un buen momento, el Sevilla está peleando por posiciones europeas y nosotros estamos bien en las tres competiciones, pero saldremos a intentar ganar desde el primer minuto". García Plaza. "Coincidimos en el Villarreal, él estaba en las inferiores y yo a cargo del primer equipo, y coincidimos también en China. Tenemos una buena relación, no es de amistad, pero le conozco desde hace tiempo y es un técnico muy capacitado". El Sevilla. "No creo que sea bueno comparar. Hay momentos y circunstancias que en los derbis tienen muchísimos factores que alteran los resultados. Estamos los dos en una temporada muy regular del Sevilla respecto a campañas anteriores y nosotros hemos intentado mantener también la estabilidad en los resultados. El partido de mañana no está condicionado a circunstancias del pasado". Técnico con más derbis. "Los planteamientos, los duelos, los derbis, son distintos cada año. Son circunstancias y plantillas distintas, pero el ambiente se mantiene, la rivalidad, que me parece muy positiva siempre que sea dentro del terreno de juego. Siempre he entendido la importancia que tiene para toda la gente del Betis ganar este derbi y, como hicimos en todas las ocasiones, buscaremos superarles". Examen. "Para la hinchada ganar todos los derbis sería muy importante. Si usted me dice ganar los derbis y ser 15º, prefiero no ganarlo y salir cuarto, quinto y jugar Champions League. Es importante tener una regularidad para conseguir logros y dentro de eso tiene que estar intentar ganar los derbis también porque sabemos que es un partido distinto para toda la hinchada". Qué Sevilla espera. "En algunos partidos estuvimos más cerca en la tabla. Los últimos no son los resultados que esperaban, pero es un equipo rocoso, con buenos jugadores, que tiene una idea de fútbol directa, que juega en su estadio, así que vamos a encontrar un Sevilla muy peligroso". Bratislava. "Se le da importancia a la Liga porque da regularidad para conseguir logros y el partido con el Sevilla tiene un plus especial. Normalmente nos centramos en el partido siguiente y una vez que terminemos el derbi veremos qué pasa el martes. Es importante para clasificar, pero después quedan tres más. Ahora pesamos solo en el derbi y veremos el domingo el mejor equipo para intentar lograr la clasificación anticipada". Cauto. "Lo más importante es que primero realicemos nuestro fútbol y a partir de ahí no sabemo cuál será el mejor jugador del Sevilla porque después los partidos son distintos. Tienen una idea de juego y tomaremos las precauciones necesarias, pero dando prioridad a lo que nosotros hacemos en un terreno de juego e intentando ser superiores". Motivación. "Cada vez que hay un derbi la semana anterior es distinta y esta lo ha sido también, con la gente buscando una alegría a través de las conversaciones, lo que uno sale a la calle y te dicen...". Más entradas. "Es un tema extradeportivo que tienen que valorar los directivos del fútbol. Hay países donde está prohibido que vaya la hinchada visitante, como en Argentina. Sabemos muchas veces las consecuencias que vienen después. Nos gustaría que la mitad fueran nuestros, pero después tocará otro derbi en nuestro estadio. No es fácil. La rivalidad le hace mucho bien a la ciudad siempre que se mantenga en el ámbito deportivo". Rotaciones. "Hay muchos parámetros para elegir el once y los cinco que entrarán después. Si no ha entrenado por lesión, puede jugar pero no estará en su mejor momento. O si ha jugado con su selección, todo el mundo puede jugar. Veremos caso por caso, los momentos de los jugadores, de los relevos, porque al final los equipos varían porque estamos en tres competiciones".

Football icon Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has said that he wants his former club Middlesbrough to finally end a decade of exile from the Premier League this season.

Boro narrowly missed out on automatic promotion last campaign after being consistently in the race before losing to a late Oli McBurnie goal in the play-off final.

Kim Hellberg's side currently sit second in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham.

In an exclusive interview with 10bet , Hasselbaink expressed his desire to see Boro return to the top flight whilst acknowledging the tough competition the club faces in the Championship.

Hasselbaink said "They've been flirting with promotion during the last three or four years. The problem that Boro have had is being able to sustain what they've built in the second half of the season.

"I would love to see them get back up there, because Boro are a special club in a really special part of the world.

"Football means everything to the people in that town, and they deserve a club in the Premier League.

"Hopefully they can sustain that momentum. Let's be honest though, as much as I would love to see them do it, it will be really, really difficult.

"The Championship is such a difficult league to get out of – Boro has been trying for almost a decade. If they can climb out of there, it will be one hell of a job because you've got West Ham, Wolves and a few others who are top, top teams."

articles.body:
Arsenal star Bukayo Saka left their UEFA Champions League game against Bayern Munich on October 21 after just 10 minutes on Wednesday at the Allianz Arena.

Saka, 25, grabbed at his upper leg following a pass against Bayern, and left the game after a few more minutes. Eberechi Eze took Saka's place in the pitch.

Arteta's initial post-match comments braced for "really bad news," and now there's more as Saka's absence nears a month and looks set to be another one.

"We had another test, he's evolving really well," said Arteta. "But it looks like it's going to be an eight-week injury, more or less. It's four at the moment, still a while for him to be back."

Bukayo Saka injury update, history: Arsenal manager Arteta to be without Saka for four more weeks

Arsenal initially had to be patient in determining a timetable due to fluid around Saka's knee in the wake of the injury. He had trouble walking without pain and was restricted in movement.

Now he faces more four weeks out of the lineup, adding to his injury woes.

Saka missed time on three different occasions last Premier League season:

The first and last of those injuries also saw him miss one Champions League league phase game at Athletic Bilbao and both legs of the quarterfinals versus Sporting Lisbon.

Arsenal have Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke featuring after letting Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli leave the club this season, so this is another opportunity for Eze or young Max Dowman to claim minutes.

articles.title: La nueva vida de Juan Mata
articles.standfirst: El ya exfutbolista se convierte en asesor a Populous, uno de los estudios de arquitectura deportiva más prestigiosos del mundo
articles.summary: El ya exfutbolista se convierte en asesor a Populous, uno de los estudios de arquitectura deportiva más prestigiosos del mundo
articles.body: Tras colgar las botas después de dos décadas de carrera —coronada con el Mundial de 2010 y etapas en clubes como el Valencia, el Chelsea o el Manchester United, además de experiencias en Japón y Australia—, Juan Mata da el salto a los despachos. El exfutbolista asturiano se incorpora como asesor a Populous, uno de los estudios de arquitectura deportiva más prestigiosos del mundo, con el objetivo de aportar “una visión estratégica y la perspectiva del propio deportista al diseño de centros de entrenamiento de élite y espacios de alto rendimiento en todo el mundo”. Su labor principal se centrará en las ciudades deportivas, un entorno que, según destaca Jorge Betancor, director general de la firma en España, para los jugadores “es su casa”. El ejecutivo deja claro el rol que desempeñará el asturiano en la compañía: “Él no va a dibujar, pero va a la mesa de decisiones”. Desde ahí ayudará a repensar unas instalaciones que los clubes entienden hoy como una inversión para “crear y cuidar talento”, apostando por un modelo más abierto que en países como Estados Unidos ya incorpora centros clínicos o usos compatibles para que “tanto el club como la comunidad se pueden beneficiar de ello”. La alianza busca aterrizar esa experiencia en aspectos muy concretos del día a día, ya que, como subraya Betancor, “son las pequeñas decisiones de diseño las que marcan la diferencia real en la experiencia de los jugadores”, poniendo como ejemplo un gimnasio de recuperación con grandes ventanales hacia el campo para mantener la motivación de los lesionados. Con la mirada puesta en los estadios de próxima generación hacia 2030, el directivo recalca que las aportaciones de Mata “van a marcar la diferencia que ningún otro equipo de arquitectos nos puede dar”, recordando que el excentrocampista ha disputado casi 200 partidos y levantado trofeos en recintos diseñados por el estudio, como el FNB Stadium de Johannesburgo o el emblemático Wembley. Este nuevo paso profesional consolida la faceta empresarial y social que el asturiano, de 38 años, lleva tiempo desarrollando lejos del césped. Más allá de su conocido compromiso solidario a través de iniciativas como Common Goal o la Right To Dream Academy, Mata amplía con esta consultoría una cartera de negocios ligada al deporte de élite en la que ya figura como inversor de la escudería Alpine de Fórmula 1, el San Diego FC de la MLS y Mercury 13, un fondo dedicado a profesionalizar clubes de fútbol femenino.

articles.title: Dowman reescribe el 'Libro Guinness de los récords'... a costa de Bellingham
articles.standfirst: La 'joya' del Arsenal se ha convertido en el jugador más joven en debutar y marcar con la sub 21 inglesa
articles.summary: La 'joya' del Arsenal se ha convertido en el jugador más joven en debutar y marcar con la sub 21 inglesa
articles.body: Max Robert Dowman (Chelmsford, 31-12-2009) parece empeñado en reescribir el 'Libro Guinness de los récords'. El joven canterano del Arsenal continúa destrozando todos los registros de precocidad habidos y por haber en las Islas. Desde que el 4 de septiembre de 2024, con 14 años y 248 días, destronara a Nathaniel Chalobah (14 años y 258 días) como el jugador más joven en representar a Inglaterra sub 17 no ha parado de reescribir la historia. Existe un 'football' antes y otro después de Dowman, tal y como se ha encargado de recordar la cuenta oficial de la Premier en 'X'. Ese mismo día desbancó también a Ethan Nwaneri (15 años y 138 días) como el goleador más precoz con la sub 17 inglesa. Su voracidad, de inmediato, se trasladó al Viejo Continente: el 19 de septiembre de 2024, con 14 años y 263 días, desbancó a Youssoufa Moukoko (14 años y 337 días) como el goleador más joven en la historia de la UEFA Youth League. Su siguiente paso fue arrebatarle dos récords a Jeremy Monga. El 1 de diciembre de 2024 se convirtió en el debutante más joven (14 años y 336 días) en la Premier League 2 y en septiembre de 2025 se erigió en el jugador más precoz (15 años y 246 días) en estrenarse con la sub 19 inglesa, de la que sólo un mes más tarde se erigió, también, en el goleador más joven (15 años y 288 días). Atrás queda ya el récord de Ryan Sessegnon. Su salto a la élite llegó el 29 de octubre de 2025, cuando desbancó a Jack Porter (16 años y 72 días) para convertirse en el jugador más joven en jugar de titular (15 años y 302 días) con el Arsenal. El resto, prácticamente, se cuenta solo: debutante más joven (15 años y 308 días) en la historia de la Champions, goleador más joven (16 años y 73 días) del Arsenal -destronó a Cesc Fàbregas- y de la propia Premier... Pero ahí no queda la cosa. También puede presumir de ser el titular más joven en Premier (16 años y 144 días) y el campeón más precoz de la Liga inglesa (16 años y 144 días). Ha aprovechado el parón para añadir otros dos nuevos récords Guinness a su palmarés... a costa de Jude Bellingham. El futbolista del Arsenal ha desbancado al madridista como el jugador más joven en jugar (16 años y 317 días) y marcar (16 años y 320 días) con la selección sub 21 inglesa. El madridista lo logró con 17 años y 67 días. Sin embargo, no se conforma. Ya tiene su próxima 'presa' entre ceja y ceja.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership preview: Celtic, Rangers, Hearts, Aberdeen
articles.summary: The Scottish Premiership returns with managers to the fore - this is all you need to know about Saturday's games.
articles.body:
The Scottish Premiership returns with an all-action Saturday after what was a bleak international break for the national side.

Most of the intrigue is on men who will not make a pass or a tackle. There is one new manager, one who is being touted for the Scotland job, another who has turned around a failing side and one who is increasingly under pressure.

And none of those are in charge of Old Firm teams. The managerial status at Celtic and Rangers is relatively settled, but of course that can change in the space of 90 minutes.

This is your essential guide to Saturday's action.

Aberdeen have a new head coach for their basement battle with Kilmarnock, with Mario Frick replacing Stephen Robinson

The Liechtensteiner was a fine striker in his day and his main mission is to get the Dons firing in front of goal again.

Frick favoured two up top while in charge of Luzern, so he needs to find a way to supply Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua.

Connor Ronan could hold the key to improving a sorry set of attacking statistics, but the Irish midfielder will need to show more than he has since his summer arrival.

Aberdeen have 12 goals from 12 league games. Kilmarnock have 13 from 13. Both sides have amassed just four points from their past six outings, so this may well be something of a scrap.

Killie were slightly more menacing in a 0-0 draw at Pittodrie in September and the same could be said of a League Cup quarter-final at Rugby Park a week later, although the Dons did well to prevail on penalties after a red card early in the second half.

The Ayrshire side have the league's worst defensive record by a distance, conceding three or more goals on six occasions. However, manager Neil McCann will have been heartened by a tenacious showing in the 1-0 loss at Celtic Park last time out.

With four successive matches coming against sides currently in the bottom six before taking on the Dundee duo, McCann will view this pre-Christmas sequence as vital.

Of the leading sides, Celtic have the easier-looking task at home to St Mirren, who have enjoyed just one victory in their past 40 visits to the east end of Glasgow in all competitions.

However, the league leaders have not kicked on since thrashing Heart of Midlothian last month, drawing with Dundee United and losing to Falkirk either side of narrow and unconvincing wins over Hibernian and Kilmarnock.

That 1-0 win at home to Killie was just a second clean sheet in seven Premiership matches for the champions.

Celtic came from behind to win 2-1 in Paisley in September, with Yang Hyun-Jun grabbing the second. The winger's return should add dynamism to their attack.

Since pushing Celtic all the way at home, St Mirren have picked up a mere four points from nine matches.

Rangers go to Motherwell off the back of a 2-0 win away to the Buddies, extending their unbeaten league run to 10 games and maintaining the best defensive numbers in the table.

The goals came from a contentious penalty and a deflected shot and manager Derek McInnes spoke of the need to sharpen up in the final third after several promising situations broke down.

After a six-game losing slump that began in Govan, Motherwell have steadied the ship and played out an entertaining 1-1 draw with Dundee United before the break that included a combined 40 efforts on goal.

Well shared the points with Rangers at Fir Park last season, scoring late on both occasions, and, while not the force they were after so many departures, still retain a core of players who celebrated victory at Ibrox in April.

Rangers have the momentum, although recent draws away to Dundee and Hearts underline the fact they remain a work in progress under McInnes.

New manager Frick to take Aberdeen back to basics

We'll only sell if offer makes club blink - McInnes

Five wins on the spin have propelled Falkirk up to third place and they will be big favourites to extend that run at home to St Johnstone.

Celtic beaten, Hearts hammered... fans are talking about European qualification, having ended a five-year stint in League 1 in May 2024.

John McGlynn continues to work his magic on a meagre budget, with new arrivals Jacob Murrell, Owen Eames, Finley Barbrook and Deniss Melniks hitting the ground running.

Ethan Ross is lapping up a new lease of life, while older heads Scott Bain and Liam Henderson have never been better, although the loss of influential skipper Brad Spencer is a huge blow.

The Perth Saints will be no pushovers. They too are punching above their weight with just four defeats in 13 on their return to the top flight.

Rangers are the only side to beat Simo Valakari's men since a 1-1 draw with Falkirk at McDiarmid Park in mid-September.

That was the first league meeting of the clubs since 2010, but, with such astute managers in place, it looks like this can remain a top-flight rivalry for a good while yet.

Have Hibs turned a corner and have Hearts fallen down a hole?

Marink Reedijk lost his first three games after replacing David Gray, but now the Hibs head coach is looking for a third successive victory at home to Dundee United.

The Easter Road side clambered out of the bottom spot in style, thumping Aberdeen 4-0 at Pittodrie after coming from behind to stun their Edinburgh rivals in the League Cup semi-final.

Hearts went into that game at Hampden as heavy favourites and across the following seven days were outplayed by the team sitting eighth in the Swiss Super League and walloped by Falkirk, ending their 19-month long unbeaten home record in the league.

A growing injury list has hampered Hearts, but Wouter Vrancken's methods are being questioned, with only Kilmarnock conceding more goals in the league.

A visit to Dundee is next and Steven Pressley's much-improved team have only been defeated once at Dens Park so far.

United have also been a breath of fresh air, adopting a new swashbuckling style that has yielded four wins and four draws in their past nine games.

Hibs have taken significant strides, particularly in the midfield area, but this will be a real test of their progress. There were 11 goals in the two games against United at Easter Road last season and another big score would not be a surprise.

articles.title: Omar Berrada interview: Manchester United chief executive on Michael Carrick, Mauricio Pochettino, recent transfer activity and the club hierarchy
articles.summary: Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has spoken exclusively to Sky Sports about the start to the season; the United CEO discusses replacing Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino, the futures of Bruno Fernandes and JJ Gabriel, transfer activity and the Man City charges
articles.body:
With United in the relegation zone, the club sacked Michael Carrick during the November international break and replaced him with Mauricio Pochettino, who will take charge of his first game away at arch-rivals Liverpool, live on Sky Sports, this Sunday.

The change in head coach has followed a tumultuous opening few months of the campaign, with Lisandro Martinez also taking aim at the club's technical director Jason Wilcox for not preparing the team well enough in the transfer window, while Fernandes also criticised Carrick and his coaching staff's methods.

In this exclusive sit-down interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Berrada discusses:

How the club accepts that a lot of the criticism at the club's leadership is fair, but some of it crosses the line

Not only why Carrick was sacked, but why United stuck with him in the summer

Why Pochettino is the right man going forwards and the "buzz" he has brought so far

How the club are defiant they have improved the United squad, despite criticism over their transfer activity

How captain Bruno Fernandes' contract talks are going and why JJ Gabriel left the club

His involvement in the Manchester City charges

Berrada believes United are going in the right direction, even though the club currently sit in the Premier League relegation zone ."One hundred per cent," he says.

"I know it's difficult to say this when you're sitting 18th in the Premier League table. It's clear - it's not good enough, not acceptable, and that's why we've made the change that we've made, so that we can move forward.

"But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently.

"The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction."

Read below to see the best of the United chief executive's interview…

'We accept the criticism - but some of it does cross the line'

This is the third season in a row in which United have changed their head coach in the middle of the season.

This season strongly resembles the 2024-25 campaign that saw United decide to stick with Erik ten Hag despite the club speaking to other potential candidates - only to replace him with Ruben Amorim a few months into the new season.

As a result, the United leadership team has been questioned - even more so after United defender Martinez publicly criticised technical director Wilcox over the transfer window just gone.

Asked if it has been difficult to see the fan criticism about the hierarchy, Berrada says: "It is. I'm not going to lie. But let's be clear, we're not the protagonists. This is not about the individuals, this is about the club.

"This is about doing everything we can to make our fans happy, and that means improving the results on the pitch, and that means getting a team that is performing to its maximum potential, that the fans can feel proud of.

"Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and the scrutiny that we're going to get. We accept it, some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.

"I think we do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that."

There are lessons to be learned as well. "If you think about the fact that we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we want to - that's for sure," Berrada adds.

"There are different circumstances as to why it didn't work out with Erik, Ruben and now Michael. And we're always learning. We're always trying to improve and understand what has failed."

However, while Berrada recognises the club's leadership hold responsibility for the club's success on and off the pitch, that responsibility also filters down to the players and coaches.

"It is our responsibility to run the club," he says. "And, yes, coaches have a very important role to play. Players, of course, have to perform at the highest level consistently for any coach.

"They're part of a club that when you're wearing the shirt, you have an enormous amount of responsibility. And that responsibility means that you have to be giving your best every day in training, in the matches. And that's the same for executives.

"So I understand the frustration from the fans. It's absolutely normal. My commitment is that we're going to do everything we can to make sure that we put ourselves in a position where we're competing to win titles consistently."

At the centre of United fan disgruntlement is the continued running of the club by the Glazer family, who work alongside INEOS chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe at the very top of the structure. Berrada insists, however, that the dual-running of the club is working.

"It's working very well," he says. "I know there's a lot of noise and people look for narratives in the media and that's fine, that comes with being part of this club.

"But from my perspective what I see is a very dedicated and engaged ownership group - both ownership groups. There's constant dialogue, we speak sometimes on a daily basis. Between them there's a very good alignment. I think they have complementary skill sets, if you want to put it that way.

"All the decisions that have been taken, we've been all on the same page, we're all supporting each other, and the shared ambition is to do what's right for the club."

Why Carrick left - and why Pochettino is the man going forwards

So how did United come to the decision to remove Carrick? The former United midfielder was talk of the town at the end of last season after qualifying the club for the Champions League - but it all unravelled quickly after that.

Many felt United would remove Carrick after the 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth on October 25, but the club waited until the international break to make their move.

"It was a very difficult decision, to be honest, especially given all the affection everyone at the club has for Michael," says Berrada.

"When he took over the team last season, they did very well under him. They were playing some really good football, winning important matches. We qualified for the Champions League and finished third.

"We felt at the time he'd earned the right to continue leading the team. So when we started the season, it's clearly been a lot more difficult than we expected. The results haven't been good enough. I think we've dropped off in many areas.

"We wanted to give ourselves until the November international break to really take stock of what was happening with the team, what were the areas that needed to be improved. And in the end, we took the decision to make a change of coach.

"Unfortunately, sometimes when you're in the middle of the season, that's the one decision that you can make that can provoke a reaction, that can provoke a change in the dynamic. So that's why we had to take the decision."

The signs about Carrick's replacement, Pochettino , are very positive, according to Berrada.

Not only has the Argentine brought a degree of positivity to the club's training ground, but the United chief executive believes he has the "maturity" to take the Old Trafford reins.

"He has a tremendous amount of passion and energy," Berrada says of Pochettino. "We see it already in the two days he's been with us.

"There's a buzz about the place, and he's brought that with his staff. He has a very clear philosophy, identity of how he wants to see the team play. And I think he's coming just at the right time for him and us to be able to help the team and take us forward.

"He's equally as ambitious as we are, which is: we want to win titles.

"You have to think that when you're playing for Manchester United, when the results aren't going well, the pressure and the scrutiny is enormous. And all that noise around the club and around the players can be difficult to manage.

"So I think in Mauricio we bring somebody that has just the right amount of maturity and experience at the big clubs to be able to put his arms around the players and to let them perform at their highest potential."

'We have depth' - Berrada defends transfer activity, including the defence

"I think we've made progress in improving the squad over the last seasons." It is certainly a bold statement from Berrada.

United spent £163m on new players this summer - the majority of that on midfielders Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

With the jury still out on that trio, a lot has been made on the lack of activity in defence. Barring the introduction of Ayden Heaven from the academy, the United backline consists of the same players who were at the club five years ago.

As a result, United have one of the worst defences in Europe's top five leagues in terms of goals conceded.

But Berrada has defended the club's transfer policy - saying the previous summer's window where they signed Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko and Senne Lammens was a successful one.

"You have to take it in the context of the last few years," he says. "The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

"When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It's probably been the summer or the transfer window where there's been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

"And we've said publicly and we've said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

"And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players that we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

"It's true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

"When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it."

United were interested in defenders this summer, most notably Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall , but Berrada insists the club were not going to overspend on players in this inflated transfer market.

"When you look at the other areas of the pitch, and there's a lot of discussion about the back line," he says.

"But we did come into it thinking: we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

"So that's why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it's been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

"I think what we've seen in the back line is we've had injuries, it's taken Matthijs de Ligt longer than we would want it to get back. Unfortunately, Luke Shaw suffered a muscle injury that meant he was out for five or six weeks.

"So could we have signed an additional defender to straighten the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

"There's no point in us spending £40m, £50m for players that we're not convinced are going to add value to the team.

"So it's always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward."

United also held interest in players such as Elliot Anderson, who moved to Manchester rivals City for £116m, and Berrada was pushed on the point about discipline in the transfer market.

"When I talk about being disciplined, I talk about not overspending on players that don't necessarily add quality to the team," he says.

"Because when you sign a player that doesn't work out for Man Utd, it becomes very difficult to move that player on or to get the sale we want. And that can set us back.

"So when I talk about being disciplined, I'm not talking about necessarily not spending to get the top players. We have the ambition to win, to win the Premier League, to win the Champions League, to win the domestic cups. And for that, we need top talent.

"So when we find the right opportunities, we will spend. But what we don't want to be doing is spending just for the sake of it."

Will Fernandes stay - and what happened with JJ Gabriel?

One of the main themes that could define Pochettino's time at United is the future of club captain Fernandes.

Sky Sports News has reported the Portuguese midfielder has turned down two new contract offers at the club, with his existing deal expiring at the end of this season.

There is a real risk the reigning Premier League and PFA Player of the Year could leave the club in the coming months.

"Listen, I've said before, we have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno," Berrada says. "We're very fortunate to have him as a captain.

"What he's done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards you can win.

"And we're very proud to have him as captain. It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private. I think it's something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club."

One player who is set to depart the club is 16-year-old talent JJ Gabriel - who announced his exit from the club this week amid an approach from Real Madrid.

United were not happy that Gabriel announced his departure without informing the club - and the entire saga has been a sour note on a club that has a long history of producing academy players.

"We did everything. Absolutely everything," says Berrada about Gabriel's situation.

"Let's not forget with JJ, he's a very young boy with a lot of media attention around him. Our primary concern is his well-being.

"Credit to the academy and people that have been here for many years, they helped him in his development. We still think this is the best place for him to continue his career and to grow.

"This club has a very rich history and tradition of developing young players and giving them the opportunity, as we're seeing this season with Shea Lacey. Obviously, Kobbie Mainoo has been doing well for us for a few years now - we're not afraid of giving young players opportunities.

"Obviously, him and his family have taken the decision to leave. We can only wish him the best.

"We want players that want to be here, that feel being at Manchester United is a privilege."

Will Berrada be affected by the Man City charges case?

Berrada was also asked about his involvement in the Manchester City charges case.

In September, an independent commission found City guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018. City are appealing against the ruling and deny any wrongdoing.

He was the chief football operations officer at City Football Group overseeing talent management, performance services and football intelligence between 2020 and 2024.

Prior to the role, Berrada had worked as chief operating officer at Man City from 2016.

"I'm not concerned," says Berrada when asked if there are any worries about his role at City.

"I want to be very clear about this: I wasn't involved in any wrongdoings. I wasn't involved in the proceedings. There are no allegations against me.

"In that sense, there will be no surprises."

But in another complication, Berrada could lead United in a compensation claim against his former club, should their appeal fail.

"I don't want to comment on that because right now, it's an ongoing process," he added.

"When it runs its course, then we'll take a view of what is our position as Manchester United."

articles.title: Mika Baur: Celtic midfielder ruled out for 'considerable' period with ankle ligament damage
articles.summary: The 22-year-old is expected to be out for at least 10 weeks; he injured his ankle in Celtic's win against Kilmarnock before the international break; Martin O'Neill's side return to Scottish Premiership action on Saturday at home to St Mirren
articles.body:
The German midfielder, who signed from Paderborn in the summer, is facing around ten weeks on the sidelines with the injury.

He left Celtic Park on crutches after he was forced off during their 1-0 win against Kilmarnock before the international break.

Manager Martin O'Neill said: "He'll be out for some considerable time. It's a real shame, he was playing great for us."

"There's talk about ten weeks, but I spoke to Mika yesterday and he's a quick healer. There are things he can't do for a while; his foot's in a boot.

"He was on fire, he was doing great for us. It is a blow and it seemed so innocuous as well.

"I thought he'd been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on and he's just gone over on it."

Celtic could also be without Benjamin Nygren for Saturday's Scottish Premiership return against St Mirren.

The midfielder missed the second of Sweden's recent double-header, with O'Neill confirming his absence from club training.

He said: "Nygren didn't train today, but we'll see how he is in the morning - he's got a sore heel. He's been feeling it for a couple of weeks."

Celtic face a gruelling five-match stretch of games over the next two weeks, with a visit to Portugal to face Torreense in the Europa League after St Mirren.

They then travel to Hearts, live on Sky Sports, before taking on Dundee at Dens Park, then a home game against St Johnstone.

The defending champions are four points ahead of Old Firm rivals Rangers at the top of the Premiership, having played a game more.

articles.title: Women's Super League: 10 games, 0 points and 30 goals conceded - why Charlton are struggling
articles.summary: BBC Sport looks at why promoted Charlton Athletic have had one of the worst starts in Women's Super League history.
articles.body:
Charlton Athletic achieved the unthinkable last season when they earned promotion to the Women's Super League - but it has been a harsh introduction.

After 10 games in the top flight, Karen Hills' side are yet to pick up a point and have scored just five goals, conceding 30.

They have already lost to the other promoted sides - Birmingham City and Crystal Palace - and are six points adrift at the bottom of the table.

The club expected a tough challenge as they made the jump up to the WSL for the first time but the results have still hit them hard.

"I'm trying everything I can," manager Hills said following their 2-0 defeat by West Ham last weekend.

That result came a week after Charlton's 3-2 loss at Crystal Palace where they had been leading with 16 minutes to go.

So is it time to consider relegation, even in November, or is there still hope for Charlton to turn things around?

Charlton pipped better resourced teams in the WSL 2 last season, eventually beating top-flight side Leicester City in a play-off to secure promotion.

An incredible 27-game unbeaten run ended in March but was founded on an effective defensive structure and often heroics by goalkeeper Sophie Whitehouse.

However, the step up has proved difficult with inexperience and tight finances standing in the way.

Statistically, Charlton rank bottom in the WSL for average possession (30%), shots on target (17), passing accuracy (66%) and successful passes (1,689).

They have conceded nine times from set-pieces - the most in the WSL - and 14 of their total goals against have come in either the first or final 15 minutes in games.

The only other sides to lose their first 10 games in a WSL season are Doncaster Rovers Belles in 2016 and Yeovil Town in 2017-18. The Belles went on to win just one game as they were relegated, while Yeovil failed to win any, drawing two and finishing bottom, only avoiding relegation because of a league restructure.

Experienced defender Ashleigh Neville, who joined Charlton from Leicester City in the summer, told BBC Sport: "We knew it was going to be a tough start to the season.

"I was really excited to embrace that challenge. It's been difficult with results but when you look at the first game compared to now, I'd like to hope that people can see we're trying to build something.

"We're trying the hardest we can off the pitch to get to terms with how quick the game is compared to the WSL 2 and the quality of players we're up against.

"But it's still a joy to come into work and people are wanting to be better, asking how they can improve and move forward."

This month, manager Hills insisted Charlton "will never throw the towel in" but admitted results are "hurting" the club.

Neville added: "It is not at the forefront of things but we've been really unlucky with the injuries that we've had in our attacking line.

"We're lacking in confidence going forward, and creativity for what we can actually provide.

"It's a vicious circle. If you haven't got confidence because you're losing games, how do you still get that confidence in games where we need it the most?"

Whitehouse's penalty masterclass sends Charlton into WSL

How WSL 2 title contenders Charlton are defying the odds

Charlton are one of only three clubs without Premier League male counterparts to offer financial backing in the WSL and that restricts their freedom in recruitment.

It has not helped that summer signing Linda Lif Boama suffered a serious knee injury in September, defender Grace Johnston was ruled out in October and Paula Partido had to return to parent club London City Lionesses for knee surgery.

Charlotte Newsham, who played a key role in their WSL 2 promotion run, was also sidelined by an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury before the play-off victory.

While Charlton sought out shrewd signings in the summer, rivals Birmingham City were able to spend six-figure sums on Manchester United duo Lisa Naalsund and Millie Turner.

The Blues also broke their club record in January - a reported £316,000 fee for Wilma Leidhammar - while Oceane Hurtre was signed last summer to boost their second-tier title hopes and has now scored seven goals in 10 WSL games.

Fellow promoted club Palace picked up four-time WSL winner Bethany England and one of the WSL 2's standout players Lexi Lloyd-Smith in the summer.

"WSL 2 teams have to be even more ready for the WSL while they're still in the WSL 2 so that when they do make that jump, it's not a huge gap," said Hills.

"The gap is continuing to get bigger and you see some of the players the top teams have brought in and the finances they have.

"It's a big challenge for us. We're finding that out on a weekly basis."

Charlton benefited from the WSL's expansion this summer to 14 teams from 12 as organisers try to bridge the gap between the leagues and to increase the number of matches.

It was well-received by fans and those within the game, but Hills says it will still take time for WSL 2 clubs to catch up.

"If you look at the bottom three teams [in the table], it's all the newly-promoted teams. The level that we're coming into is already very well established."

Neville added: "I think the financial side plays a massive part. We do our bit where we can. But it's hard to bring in the experienced players you need."

articles.title: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani tore his Achilles while playing soccer, says he'll be in a boot for 6-8 weeks
articles.summary: 'I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35.'
articles.body:
Even mayors aren't immune to season-ending injuries. On Friday, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that he had torn an Achilles tendon during a soccer game against the press corps.

Mamdani revealed the injury as part of a news conference to announce that he would be closing Rikers Island jail . The mayor arrived to the podium on crutches, with a boot on his right leg.

The friendly match against the press took place on Thursday, with Mamdani saying that his team won the game 10-5. The injury, which was reportedly non-contact, occurred during the second half of the match, while Mamdani was running for the ball on the indoor turf field.

When pressed by a member of the media, Mamdani, who reportedly arrived late to the game, admitted that he did not stretch before taking the field.

"I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35. And soon after, I tore my Achilles," Mamdani said during the press conference.

The mayor will have to wear a boot for six-to-eight weeks, he said, adding that he anticipates being able to play soccer again in nine months.

Mamdani, who is a noted soccer fan and has been known to play pickup throughout his time as mayor, has been involved in multiple soccer initiatives since going into office. With New Jersey's MetLife Stadium holding games in the World Cup this summer, Mamdani negotiated with FIFA to secure 1,000 $50 tickets for New Yorkers. Mamdani has done similar affordability initiatives with local NWSL team Gotham FC, first in April , and then again for the first round of the playoffs earlier this month.

articles.title: Tom Brady Reportedly Buys Chelsea Ownership Stake After Birmingham City Exit
articles.summary: NFL icon Tom Brady is adding a Premier League club to his investment portfolio after divesting his stake in Birmingham City.
articles.body:
NFL icon Tom Brady is adding a Premier League club to his investment portfolio after divesting his stake in Birmingham City.

According to ESPN and NFL Network , Brady has purchased shares in Chelsea Football Club. The Guardian 's Matt Hughes first reported Brady was in discussions to acquire a stake in the Premier League power.

The news comes weeks after Brady gave up his minority stake in Birmingham City, which currently leads the EFL Championship table.

Report: Vanessa Bryant, Pau Gasol Eyeing Sparks Ownership

Brady has also held minority stakes in the Las Vegas Aces and Las Vegas Raiders since 2023 and 2024, respectively.

Hughes reported Brady's decision to sell his stake in Birmingham was made "to pave the way" for the investment in Chelsea.

The news comes just over a month after Chelsea announced former majority owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter had sold their controlling stakes to a private equity firm led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano.

Hughes reported Brady "is understood to have a good relationship" with Eghbali.

Brady bought his reported 3.3 percent share in Birmingham in August 2023, just months after his final retirement from the NFL.

His tenure spanned Birmingham's relegation to League One in 2024, which was followed by its return to the Championship in 2025 and aspirations of a Premier League bid in 2027.

The Athletic's Gregg Evans reported after Brady's exit he had last attended a Birmingham game in April 2025.

Evans noted Brady's split from the club was in part because his broadcasting contract with FOX "places restrictions on travel during the busy months of the English football season."

"Sources say he still provided assistance when needed and even appeared on calls to help new signings over the line, but he was never setting club strategies or assisting with manager Chris Davies' matchday plans," Evans reported.

articles.title: Chelsea fined £150,000 by FA for discriminatory chanting
articles.summary: Chelsea are fined £150,000 by the FA for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chants during their FA Cup third-round win at Charlton in January.
articles.body:
Chelsea have been fined £150,000 by the Football Association as part of a punishment for anti-Catholic and anti-Irish chants during an FA Cup third-round win at Charlton Athletic in January.

The club have also been warned about their future conduct and had an action plan imposed on them in relation to the offence.

"Chelsea FC failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief," said an FA statement. , external

Chelsea admitted the charge but had an appeal against the fine issued by an independent regulatory commission rejected.

The FA's written reasons stated that although the discriminatory chanting "lasted approximately one minute and was not repeated, the scale of participation was a significant aggravating feature".

"We unequivocally condemn this behaviour," said a Chelsea statement. , external "Sectarian abuse - chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group - and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

"Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary."

The FA itself was fined by Uefa for a similar incident of chanting, from England's away support during their Nations League victory in Spain on Sunday.

articles.title: Luis Díaz compite con Messi, Mbappé y Haaland por ser el mejor delantero en los Globe Soccer Awards 2026
articles.standfirst: Luis Díaz, nominado a Mejor Delantero en los Globe Soccer Awards 2026: cómo votar y quiénes compiten
articles.summary: Luis Díaz, nominado a Mejor Delantero en los Globe Soccer Awards 2026: cómo votar y quiénes compiten
articles.body: El extremo guajiro Luis Díaz suma un nuevo espaldarazo a su trayectoria internacional tras ser incluido entre los nominados al premio Best Forward (Mejor Delantero) de los Globe Soccer Awards 2026, una distinción en la que compite frente a algunas de las máximas figuras del fútbol mundial como Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland y Lamine Yamal. La noticia llega pocas semanas después de que el colombiano figurara en la carrera por el Balón de Oro y consolida su impacto en su etapa con el Bayern de Múnich. La categoría de Mejor Delantero de la 17.ª edición de los Globe Soccer Awards reúne a 14 atacantes de primer nivel en el panorama internacional. Además de Díaz, Mbappé, Messi, Haaland y Yamal, el listado incluye a Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Raphinha, Vinícius Júnior, Julián Álvarez, Lautaro Martínez, Ousmane Dembélé, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia y Bukayo Saka. Para el fútbol colombiano, ver a Luis Díaz compartiendo terna con referentes generacionales y jóvenes estrellas del planeta confirma que su salto y consolidación en Alemania lo mantienen en la élite ofensiva. Su presencia también refleja el peso del proyecto del Bayern de Múnich en esta edición de los premios, ya que el club bávaro aparece nominado a Mejor Club Masculino de 2026 y su técnico, Vincent Kompany, figura entre los candidatos a Mejor Entrenador. El respaldo a la nominación del atacante colombiano se apoya tanto en el éxito colectivo alcanzado en Alemania como en su producción ofensiva y su aporte en el esquema del club: Dominio doméstico con el Bayern de Múnich: En su primera temporada con el conjunto muniqués, Díaz conquistó los tres grandes trofeos del fútbol alemán —Bundesliga, DFB Pokal y Supercopa de Alemania— y el equipo alcanzó las semifinales de la Liga de Campeones de la UEFA. Números ofensivos destacados: Los reportes señalan una campaña de alto impacto estadístico para el extremo en Europa, con 26 goles y una producción de asistencias que los distintos reportes sitúan entre 19 y 23 según el corte estadístico, además de superar los 50 partidos y los 4.000 minutos disputados en todas las competencias. Socio en un ataque de peso: Bajo la conducción de Vincent Kompany, Díaz formó parte de un frente ofensivo de enorme jerarquía junto a figuras como Harry Kane y Michael Olise, también considerados entre los mejores delanteros del ciclo. Presencia con la Selección Colombia: Su año también incluyó actividad con el combinado nacional, sumando apariciones en la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2026 con goles y asistencias registradas en el ciclo. A diferencia de galardones definidos exclusivamente por gremios especializados como el Balón de Oro, los Globe Soccer Awards combinan la participación del público con el criterio de un jurado oficial designado por la organización: Primera fase abierta al público: La votación popular está habilitada en el portal oficial (vote.globesoccer.com) desde el 18 de noviembre hasta el 30 de noviembre de 2026. Los seguidores que elijan a Luis Díaz deben ingresar al sitio, ubicar la categoría Best Forward y emitir su voto. Finalistas y decisión mixta: Los candidatos más votados avanzan a la siguiente etapa, donde el resultado final conjuga el respaldo de los aficionados con la evaluación del jurado sobre el desempeño de los futbolistas a lo largo de 2026. Termómetro inicial: De acuerdo con el reporte de Semana, en los primeros compases de la encuesta pública Kylian Mbappé lidera con amplia ventaja (alrededor del 45 %), seguido a distancia por nombres como Erling Haaland, Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane y Lionel Messi, mientras Luis Díaz marcha con un 0,6 % inicial, un margen que aún puede moverse durante los días restantes de votación abierta. La ceremonia oficial de entrega de la 17.ª edición de los Globe Soccer Awards se celebrará el 28 de diciembre de 2026 en Dubái, Emiratos Árabes Unidos, fecha en la que se conocerá quién se queda con el trofeo al mejor delantero del año.

articles.title: El CEO del United: "Hicimos todo, absolutamente todo, para retener a JJ Gabriel"
articles.standfirst: "Obviamente, él y su familia han tomado la decisión de marcharse. Solo podemos desearle lo mejor. Queremos jugadores que quieran estar aquí, que sientan que estar en el Manchester United es un privilegio", ha dicho Omar Berrada en Sky Sports
articles.summary: "Obviamente, él y su familia han tomado la decisión de marcharse. Solo podemos desearle lo mejor. Queremos jugadores que quieran estar aquí, que sientan que estar en el Manchester United es un privilegio", ha dicho Omar Berrada en Sky Sports
articles.body: Omar Berrada, CEO del Manchester United, ha explicado la postura del club sobre JJ Gabriel en una entrevista en Sky Sports. El jugador de 16 años, una de las grandes perlas del fútbol mundial, ya ha dicho adiós esta semana a los red devils, club en el que se ha formado desde 2020, con un vídeo en sus redes sociales. Un gesto que confirma lo que MARCA ha ido detallando en los últimos tiempos. Su salida del United es ya un hecho y su firma por el Real Madrid está al caer. A todo lo que ha ocurrido en los últimos días se ha referido Berrada. "Hicimos todo, absolutamente todo, para retener a JJ Gabriel. No olvidemos que JJ es un chico muy joven y que hay mucha atención mediática a su alrededor. Nuestra principal preocupación es su bienestar", dijo en Sky Sports. "Hay que reconocer el mérito de la cantera y de las personas que llevan aquí muchos años, que le han ayudado en su desarrollo. Seguimos pensando que este es el mejor lugar para que continúe su carrera y siga creciendo", continuó y apostilló: "No tenemos miedo de dar oportunidades a los jóvenes". Berrada reconoció que con JJ Gabriel ya no había vuelta atrás. El jugador estaba seguro del nuevo camino que iba a emprender: "Obviamente, él y su familia han tomado la decisión de marcharse. Solo podemos desearle lo mejor. Queremos jugadores que quieran estar aquí, que sientan que estar en el Manchester United es un privilegio". Otro de los temas a los que se refirió el CEO de los red devils es a la situación de Bruno Fernandes: "Somos muy afortunados de tenerlo como capitán. Lo que ha hecho por este equipo en los últimos seis o siete años es absolutamente increíble. Es cierto que estamos hablando sobre su nuevo contrato, pero prefiero mantenerlo en privado. Creo que es algo que debe discutirse entre él y el club, en privado".

articles.title: Owono se deja ver por primera vez para asistir al homenaje a Demi en Andorra
articles.standfirst: El portero, con cara de tristeza, quiso estar en la grada de Encamp en el acto que hizo su club
articles.summary: El portero, con cara de tristeza, quiso estar en la grada de Encamp en el acto que hizo su club
articles.body: El Andorra, en su regreso al Encamp para disputar un partido, rindió un emotivo homenaje a la figura de Jesús de Miguel 'Demi'. Los jugadores salieron al verde con camisetas con su dorsal y nombre y, a ellos, acompañaba un ramo de flores blancas. Asimismo, se guardó un respetuoso minuto de silencio. Lo más significativo fue ver en la grada del estadio tricolor al meta Jesús Owono junto a compañeros no convocados y situado entre los lesionados Álex Calvo y Le Normand. Y es que, Owono quiso salir de su casa, dejarse ver en público por primera vez para asistir al homenaje a Demi. Mientras que todo el público le saludaba y sus compañeros le arropaban, la cara llena de tristeza del meta no cambiaba. Vestido de color oscuro y con un gorro negro, Owono rezó nada más acabar el minuto de silencio. Hay que recordar que el meta pidió ver a la familia de Jesús de Miguel días atrás y es una cosa que pide poder hacer algún día.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Manchester United head coach discusses drone footage, his approach to data and Bruno Fernandes ahead of first game
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has spoken out on his training session being leaked by drone footage, Bruno Fernandes and his side's running data; watch Liverpool vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports Premier League from 4pm on Sunday; kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
A 12-minute video taken over United's Carrington training ground showed the Argentine overseeing various tactical drills with his new team as they prepared for a trip to Anfield on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

The operator has since apologised and taken down the video, but footage has been viewed over eight million times on reposts from other X accounts and has since been reuploaded by several other YouTube channels, collectively attracting hundreds of thousands of views.

Sky Sports News understands the club do not plan on taking legal action, but will not rule out doing so in the future if further incidents occur, and Pochettino questioned the motivation behind the filming.

"What are you going to find?" Pochettino said in an exclusive interview with Sky Sports . "We have young guys training with us. It’s not nice. It’s not good.

"What do they want to show? Yes, we were working on shape. We were very organised. What is the point of doing something that can be very dangerous?

"I don't want to be upset, but I think it's a process the club is caring a lot about. For sure, something will happen."

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola admitted that he was sent the footage after it was released, but said that the act should've been illegal.

"They sent me it yesterday, the footage. But the important part of this is it shouldn't be legal," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference.

"Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes of our training. You know who trained with us, you know who didn't train but it's not a matter of the advantage. It's the fact someone can do this.

"There is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club."

'Head coach? Manager? The title doesn't matter'

Away from the training footage, Pochettino was quizzed on how much influence he wants to have over the club as he looks to become the man to finally restore glory at Old Trafford.

The Argentine has officially been appointed as head coach, the same as predecessors Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. That was a point of contention from the former during the final press conference before his sacking, as he defiantly labelled himself the manager.

However, the term doesn't bother Pochettino as he still hopes to be involved in all the key decisions as time progresses.

"I know that I'm the head coach. I am the guy who is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I'm going to pick the starting XI," he said.

"I'm going to make the changes, and of course, in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen in the squad.

"Sometimes I worked much better when I was head coach or when I was coach than manager.

"It's not necessarily the case that if you are manager, you make all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and you have more power in the decisions. It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, the relationship, with all the areas there."

Captain Bruno remains very important to Poch

Another point of contention at United remains the future of club captain Bruno Fernandes.

The PFA Player of the Year has struggled with his form this season and his contract at Old Trafford is due to run out at the end of the season.

The club do hold an optional one-year extension, and CEO Omar Berrada has confirmed that the club remain in discussions over a new deal for the Portuguese international.

Pochettino confirmed his intentions to keep Fernandes as captain and stressed his importance.

"Bruno is our captain, and I think he's a very important player, but all the players need to feel that they are important, from the top to the bottom or from the bottom to the top," he said.

"But Bruno is our captain and he is a very important player. I think we will have time afterwards to talk about the things that you ask me."

Poch keen to improve data as running stats called into question

In terms of what is on his immediate agenda, Pochettino is focusing on improving the data metrics across the club.

"When we arrived, I think we found a group of players and we proposed the football that we feel [is the best]. That's being brave, being Man Utd. I think it is about proposing that idea, and they revise it; it is to be brave and try to bring that to the field.

"I need to be honest, sometimes data shows something that you can then see on the field. We are going to be very focused and try to improve our data, our numbers, in every single area of the field.

"We are here not to denounce things. We are here to build something with our players and with the club, and try to perform and win games."

United's running and intensity off the ball has been a major criticism of them throughout the season, with former boss Carrick flippantly saying of his players after their 4-1 defeat to Como in October "whatever tactics you play, if you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

However, Pochettino does believe that context has to be taken into account when it comes to the underlying data about his United side.

"I see that is a debate that I don't like to go in because I think we cannot talk about things without context, and data is about context," he added.

"If you don't put context on the data, I think it's very dangerous to talk, and I think that it's easy to manipulate the data."
